chunks: Indeed, Allah, there is no god but Him, when He prohibited charity for us, He sent down khums for us. So charity is forbidden to us, khums is an obligation for us, and honor-gifts are permissible for us.

key_terms.الصَّدَقَةَ: charity; here, alms made forbidden for them
key_terms.الْخُمُسَ: khums; the one-fifth due ordained for them
key_terms.الْكَرَامَةُ: honor-gifts or dignified presents given lawfully
key_terms.حَرَامٌ: forbidden and not lawful to take
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٌ: an obligatory due established by Allah

ai.seo_question: Why is ṣadaqah forbidden for the Ahl al-Bayt while khums is lawful for them?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that when Allah prohibited ṣadaqah for the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام, He legislated khums for them instead. The hadith establishes a legal distinction between forbidden charity, obligatory khums, and permissible honorary gifts.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1649 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"Indeed, Allah (swt), there is no god but Him, when He prohibited charity (Sadaqah) for us, He ordained Khums for us. Thus, charity is forbidden to us, Khums is an obligation for us, and gifts of honor are permissible for us."
